Hi fitness. I've been getting in shape over the last 6 months, and am down to the point where my upper abdominals are fully visible. I estimate (with a caliper) that my body fat is somewhere in the 13-15% range.

It's really frustrating me that I can't lose the last bit of fat in my lower midriff to reveal all of my abs. I'm on about 10 cal/pounds at ~160 lbs and I'm 6'1" 1/2.

Any advice? Do I just need to stop being impatient wuss and kick up the HIIT? I do it twice a week (the other three days are strength) as of now.

Edit: I forgot to mention that I've managed to get some tendonitis in my hip area that restricts my ability to do situps, captains' chairs, etc. So I've been doing weighted planks and pelvic thrusts. Any other suggestions?
Abs Frustration: Down to ~13.5% body fat but can't seem to lose the last bit.
Probably you could combine it with some targeted ab work and just be a bit more patient. Plus finding that perfect lighting spot goes a long way as well.

This is exactly what I'm thinking, at 6'2" and 160 lbs he may just not have much ab to show. Try going out of cut mode for a while, bulking up some, hitting some dragon flags and hanging leg raises while you're at it, and then trying again, OP. People store fat differently, but personally I can see my abs pretty darn well at 13% bf as measured with calipers, and I'm quite a bit heavier for my height than you are. People like to say abs are all about low bodyfat, but in reality abdominal development definitely plays a role in it.

Yeah, you're right, I don't have tons to show. But I can see definition in my upper abs, so I've got some. I'd just like to get down to ~10% body fat so that I can see the results of what I've done so far. I have been doing quite a lot of core work (above and beyond leg and arm work) as everyone that I've talked to that seems to know anything prioritizes core above everything else. Thanks for the advice.

OK, well I wouldn't kick up the HIIT to more than twice a week, you'll just wear yourself out. Try adding some long walks after your strength workouts and/or on the weekends, to get your caloric expenditure up. And maybe add a fast day, with a couple of protein shakes to preserve lean body mass.
Alright, I'll try that out once I get to university (it's about 100 degrees where I am now). Thanks!

Alright. Thanks.

I forgot to add...I have some sort of tendonitis in my hip area that's tied to lower abdominal contractions, so I've got to be off it for 3 more weeks. (Things I can't do: Situps, particularly decline situps, and captain's chairs). Any specific exercises that you can think of that get around this? I do crunches with weights, weighted planks, and pelvic thrusts (none of which irritate my injury).

It's all going to come down to diet. Doesn't matter how much HIIT or whatever you do if your diet is shit. Spend more time fixing your diet and really counting your calories before you spend any more time at the gym (more than you already are, that is). Ab work isn't necessarily going to make your abs show up, unless your abs are just totally undertrained.

And then there's just plain genetics and the reality of what abs are. Those guys you see in movies and in magazines do not have real abs. They're either CGI enhanced or they go through absolute torture to shred down to dangerous levels of body fat and hydration levels to get the saran-wrap effect, which lasts just a few days before going back to normal. On the genetics side of things, your body may just really want to keep the fat stores covering your abs, so you might never be able to get rid of them on a long term basis. Shit happens.
glad you said it, I cringe when I hear someone give advise like "just do more ab work"
